title: getting-started's first tree shows three things intent init does not create, and one nothing on the page creates
body:
`docs/getting-started.md` §1 prints a five-entry tree as what `intent init` creates. Three of the five entries are not created by `intent init`, and one of them is not created by any step of the page. The prose above the tree compounds it: it says `intent init` *generates the agent contract at the root*, and it does not.

## Driven

On a machine scrubbed of every confounder AC-02.1 names -- scratch `$HOME`, `PATH` without `~/.local/bin`, `INTENT_HOME` unset, install root from `git archive` (no `.git`, so no hooks), `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`SYSTEM` redirected. Positive control: `command -v intent` returned NOT FOUND before the install root's binary was put on `PATH`.

Immediately after `git init` + `intent init`, against the page's own tree:

    intent/.config/config.json   present
    intent/st/                   MISSING
    intent/docs/                 MISSING
    intent/wip.md                present
    AGENTS.md (root)             MISSING

What `intent init` actually wrote, from its own output: `intent/.config/config.json`, `.prettierignore`, `CLAUDE.md`, `intent/.intentfiles`, `intent/llm/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `intent/llm/DECISION_TREE.md`, `intent/llm/RULES.md`, `intent/wip.md`.

**`intent/st/` arrives with the first `intent st new`**, re-measured after §2 and present from then on. **`intent/docs/` is never created by anything on the page** -- still absent after the complete journey through §7. **`AGENTS.md` arrives with `intent agents sync`**, which the page mentions only in its closing paragraph, as an aside about coding agents, long after the tree has told the reader it is already there.

## Why this is the class AC-02.1 was rewritten to catch

**This repository has `intent/docs/`.** The tree was transcribed from a mature project rather than observed from a fresh one, which is AC-02.1's own sentence -- *an install page written by someone who is installed cannot discover what it assumes* -- reproducing on the first command of the page it governs. No proofread finds it: every path named is real, correctly spelled, and correctly described. Only the timing is wrong, and timing is exactly what a read cannot check.

## Fix shape

The tree is not wrong about the project, it is wrong about the moment. Either show what `intent init` actually writes and introduce `st/` and `AGENTS.md` at the steps that create them, or keep one tree and label it as the shape a project reaches rather than the shape `init` leaves. The second is fewer words and loses the thing worth having: the reader's next command is `intent st new`, and a tree that already shows `st/` gives them nothing to notice when it appears.

Whichever is chosen, the prose sentence must lose *and generates the agent contract at the root*, or move to wherever `agents sync` is introduced.

## Not this issue

`0192` (`st edit` hands back a generated view's path) and `0193` (`st edit design` on a new thread) are separate, open, and were both re-confirmed on the same drive. §5's warning that `at green --help` says *reachable only from red* is stale -- the phrase is not in the help -- and is small enough to fold into whichever edit lands here.
